newsitem.title: USA: Rockwell CEO sees 15 pct annual EPS growth.
newsitem.headline: Rockwell CEO sees 15 pct annual EPS growth.

text.p: Rockwell International Corp Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Donald Beall said Wednesday he expects earnings per share growth to average 15 percent annually "indefinitely."

Beall, speaking to reporters after a special shareholder meeting, said the company's focus in automation, electronics and the automotive industries should leave it generating $1.5 billion in annual cash flow by the year 2000.
At the meeting, shareholders approved the sale of Rockwell's aerospace and defense businesses to Boeing Co.

For the fiscal year ended September 30, 1996, Rockwell reported income from continuing operations of $3.11 a share, before a $0.56 acquisition charge related to Brooktree Corp, on sales of $10.4 billion from continuing operations.
The $defense and aerospace business, sold to Boeing in a deal valued at $3.2 billion, including debt assumption, was reported as a discontinued operation.

Fiscal 1996 results were propelled by Rockwell's semiconductor equipment unit, which makes modem components and other computer and communications gear. Beall said the present fiscal year would be aided by avionics and automation results.

"The demonstrated track record of our four ongoing leadership businesses gives us great confidence we can achieve our goals of eight percent average annual sales growth and 15 percent average annual EPS growth going forward," Beall said at the shareholder meeting.
He said he expects return on equity to increase to "20 plus percent" in the year 2000 from the 14 percent reported in 1996.
